original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Decide whether the unsigned F3 seven-source connector (seven immutable sources, all 127 nonzero binary-mask outputs, one arbitrarily dirty restored connector) attains the 402-call floor of three calls per operator.
scope_change_reason: Keeps the F3 alphabet and answers PR4232's open question 1, a source-count question the card lists as a scope-change trigger. With PR4232's deletion lemma it fixes the exact batch size up to which an F3 connector pays three calls per operator.
bottleneck_link: Bounds the largest batch at which an F3 connector consumer can pay exactly three calls per operator: six sources. No physical consumer, admission or transfer is supplied, so no kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop after the exhaustive n=7 census with two engines and the n<=6 and brute-force calibrations. Exact optima for n>=8 are left open.
evidence: Two separately written C enumerators check every restored 21-event path up to rotation and relabelling; neither finds a path serving all 127 masks. CERTIFICATE.json records per-shard leaf counts and n<=6 calibration counts; verify.py cross-checks both reductions against a pure-Python brute force for n<=4 and re-checks PR4232's 405-call word.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact optimum for each n=8..13?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A consumer of a larger F3 batch needs the exact surcharge; only floor+3 is known as a lower bound.
open_questions.first_step: Search for words whose source path serves all but a few masks with triples and pays six readouts for the rest, then bound the number of triple-served masks.
open_questions.blocked_by: No upper or lower bound beyond floor+3 is proved for n>=8.

open_questions.question: What is the maximum number of masks a seven-source 21-event path serves with readout triples?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It bounds how many outputs need longer readout lists in any near-floor word.
open_questions.first_step: Extend reduced.c to record the maximum served count instead of exiting at the first unserved mask.
open_questions.blocked_by: The census exits early and records only the decision.

open_questions.question: Is there a short written proof that no seven-source floor path exists?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace a 4e9-path census and might explain where the threshold sits.
open_questions.first_step: Apply PR4232's window form to the all-ones mask and the seven weight-six masks.
